home.title: Zinc
home.h1a: Write it once. Run it natively
home.lead: Desktop and mobile apps the way Electron makes them, without shipping a browser. UI, games, 3D, video and hardware, from one strict, typed subset of TypeScript and JSX, from a Mac to an ESP32.
home.brew: With Homebrew, on macOS or Linux: nothing to compile. brew update && brew upgrade zinc installs each new release.
home.heroalt: The hero demo: an app with an intro, screens, transitions and a gallery
home.why.h: Fast to start, small to ship, wide to run.
home.feats: Interpreted while you work, compiled to C++ when you ship: one executable, no JavaScript engine or browser inside.
Plain JavaScript and npm packages run on QuickJS (built in), JavaScriptCore, V8 or Hermes: one flag, the same program, plugins and WebGL.
A Mac, Windows, Linux, every Raspberry Pi, a reMarkable, an HP TouchPad from 2011, an ESP32, a PS2.
zinc dev swaps each save into the running app: the window and the state stay, the page you were on, what you typed, the round in progress.
One zinc command builds, runs, debugs, tests, packages and flashes. Cross builds need no Docker and no SDK.
Solid or React models, Tailwind-like classes, a shadcn-style kit, Nuxt UI 4 and React Native components, on a GPU renderer.
fetch, WebSocket, crypto.subtle, localStorage, and the battery, sensors, vibration and notifications of the device.
three.js, video, sound, MIDI, maps, physics, SQLite, Sonos, Spotify, and drivers for LED matrices, e-ink and OLED screens.
home.every.h: From a desktop app to a microcontroller.
home.every.lead: The same engine and the same language. Cross builds use a pinned zig toolchain that zinc toolchain downloads.
home.eng.h: Bring your JavaScript, pick the engine.
home.eng.lead: Typed Zinc compiles to native code. Plain JavaScript runs on the engine you choose with --engine or "engine" in zinc.json, unchanged. Every engine is bound through Node-API, so plugins, WebGL and WebAssembly are written once; the engines you do not use are downloaded, signed and checked, only when a program asks for them.
home.engines: nothing to download on a Mac, Safari inspector
experimental; fast start from bytecode, no JIT needed
home.cli.rows: start a project from one of 13 templates (game, 3D, dashboard, IoT, e-ink, service...)
run it, with Fast Refresh and a DevTools inspector
run plain JavaScript (three.js, PixiJS, Phaser) as it is
set breakpoints in VS Code or Chrome
test on the interpreter, in native code, on QuickJS or a simulated device
home.note: Zinc has been a project of several years, and of many failures. It exists today thanks to intensive help from AI; the direction, the design choices and the tests on real hardware stay human. Read the whole note.
start.title: Get started
start.description: Install Zinc, check the machine with zinc doctor, create a project, edit it with Fast Refresh, build for another target and flash a board.
start.lead: One command with Homebrew, nothing to compile. Or build it from the sources: CMake 3.20+ and a C++20 compiler, nothing else (the libraries are vendored, Node.js is not needed).
start.install.p: On macOS or Linux (x86_64 or aarch64), with Homebrew: the prebuilt zinc of the latest release, its SHA-256 checked, on your PATH. brew update && brew upgrade zinc installs each new release.
start.install.src: On Windows, or to work on Zinc itself, build from the sources ({sources}): CMake 3.20+ and a C++20 compiler, see the guide.
start.doctor.p: The engine, this machine's renderer, the tools it downloads by itself the day you build for a board, and the plugins.
start.new.p: zinc new --list prints the 13 templates: game, game-2d, 3d, desktop-app, dashboard, cli, server, service, iot, iot-board, eink, remarkable, plugin.
start.run.p: A window opens. The first run compiles for this machine and takes a few seconds, the next ones start at once.
start.dev.p: Watches the project and swaps every save into the running program: the window stays, and so does the state (the page you were on, what you typed, the game round in progress). Only the files you changed run again, and a component you edit renders again in place. When a change cannot be swapped (a native plugin, a module with a side effect it cannot undo), it restarts and says why in one line. A compile error is a red box on the screen. UI programs get the Chrome DevTools inspector. None of this is in what zinc build ships.
start.targets: Raspberry Pi 3, 4 and 5 (64-bit), reMarkable Paper Pro
every 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS, Pi 1 and Zero included
flashes the board, or runs it in Espressif's QEMU
start.flash.p: Uses the pinned esptool. Without a board, zinc run --simulate hp-touchpad and the ESP32 QEMU runner let you try a device you do not have.
